headline: Live Vocabulary Upgrade Game for ESL Classes
problemStatement: Students often know words on a quiz—but when they write or speak, they reach for the same basic vocabulary. Vocab Sprint trains better word choice in context, fast, with instant feedback the class can learn from.
outcomes: Upgrade vague words ("good", "nice", "thing", "do") into more precise choices inside real sentences
Practice register (formal vs casual) by choosing words that fit the situation
Build speed: make a better word choice in under 30 seconds
Learn from the leaderboard + examples: why one word fit better than another
howItWorks: Pick a topic and difficulty; the game generates short sentences with intentionally weak words
Students replace one weak word with a stronger option (phone/tablet browser)
Scoring is immediate: accuracy + fit + precision (not exact-match only)
Project the round: discuss 1–2 top answers, then move on
teacherUseCases: Pre-writing: run 2–3 rounds before a paragraph task to prime vocabulary
Revision day: use topics from the writing you’re currently grading

faq.q: Can I align this to my unit topic?
faq.a: Yes. Use your unit terms as the topic (e.g., "jobs", "space", "environment"). You’ll get new sentences each time, so you can repeat it across lessons without repeats.
No. They join with a code/link and submit from a browser. This is designed for classrooms with minimal setup.

faq.q: How do I run it with a big class?
faq.a: Run ‘everyone submits’ rounds, then project the top 3 answers and discuss them. If you want more speaking, have pairs justify why their word fits better.

faq.q: What level does it work for?
faq.a: A2+ is the sweet spot. For lower levels, keep topics concrete and difficulty low; for higher levels, use abstract topics and push for register/nuance.

faq.q: Will it accept different correct words?
faq.a: Yes. It rewards fit. Two students can get points with different words if both make the sentence stronger and still correct.

faq.q: How long should a session be?
faq.a: 10–15 minutes is ideal: enough repetition to build the habit without dragging.
